content:
noah (People Ops): Quick convo: managers asking about visibility into promo calibration decisions and audit logs. Wanted to document the policy and what managers can request.

jake (Eng Manager): We got a request from someone asking why their promo was denied. They asked for the committee notes. What do we share?

noah (People Ops): Short answer: we share the manager narrative and the list of objective evidence used. We do NOT share private committee deliberations or individual reviewer comments.

anya (IC): If I ask for an audit of the process (to check for inconsistencies), can I get anonymized committee feedback?

noah (People Ops): You can request an audit. Outcome: People Ops will provide an anonymized summary of calibration criteria applied, the evidence considered, and whether any policy exceptions were used. We won't release reviewer IDs or verbatim internal chat.

hr-audit-bot: :mag_right: Audit request received. Expected turnaround: 5 business days. Submit form: https://go.company/promo-audit-request

jake (Eng Manager): For managers, what's acceptable to escalate? We want to avoid endless appeals.

tara (Director): Escalation guidance: appeal only if there is new, material evidence or a process error (e.g., missing documentation, misapplied band rules). Manager-led reconciliation first (1 paragraph), then People Ops review. Appeals must be filed within 14 days of original outcome.

noah (People Ops): We also log final decisions and the evidence packet used (PR links, dashboards, peer notes). Managers can request a copy for their records. That copy is marked as "confidential - internal HR use".

anya (IC): Timeline question: if an appeal succeeds and comp is adjusted retroactively, how is retro pay handled?

noah (People Ops): Retro comp follows payroll rules. If approved before payroll cutoff, adjustment will be in next run; otherwise next cycle. We may split large retro amounts. We'll include tax implications in the approval email.

jake (Eng Manager): Can we get a standard template for manager reconciliation to speed appeals?

noah (People Ops): Yes. Use this short template (copy into nomination/appeal):
```
- Case summary: (1-2 lines)
- New evidence: (links + 1-line context)
- Why policy error or new impact: (1-2 lines)
- Requested outcome: (title/comp/equity)
- Director sign-off: (name)
```

tara (Director): Also a note on transparency: we should publish a public (company-wide) FAQ about what is and isn't shareable. Keeps expectations aligned.

noah (People Ops): Agreed. I'll draft the FAQ and a short manager-facing checklist explaining what documentation we keep and for how long. Retention: evidence packets are retained for 2 years per HR policy, anonymized stats retained longer for fairness analytics.

hr-audit-bot: :white_check_mark: Appeal window reminder set for 14 days from decision.

anya (IC): If a manager submits conflicting peer feedback, does that count as new evidence on appeal?

noah (People Ops): It can, if it's material and wasn't available during the original review. Manager should include reconciliation + direct links. Committee will re-evaluate only if it changes the objective evidence set.

jake (Eng Manager): One edge case: compensation bands changed during the review period. How do we treat those?

noah (People Ops): We use the band effective date that was active at the time of decision. If bands later shift materially and someone appeals, People Ops may consider market-adjusted remediation, but it's a separate people-ops comp process (not a retro appeal of the original committee).

tara (Director): Final practical: please route any urgent retention cases to me + noah via DM and tag "urgent-promo" in the form. We'll fast-track triage.

noah (People Ops): Thanks. I'll post the manager reconciliation template + the draft FAQ in the promo toolkit and link here. Let's keep appeals limited to material cases to avoid overload.

hr-audit-bot: :pushpin: Promo toolkit updated: https://go.company/promo-toolkit (audit FAQ + manager template added)
